svg.title: One intrinsic trace on the original crossed linking algebra
svg.desc: The two-step first-metric tangent density and the original vertical Haar density supply a faithful semifinite trace on the reduced crossed linking algebra. Both actual corners are restrictions of the same trace. Compact smooth pair kernels have summable product Fourier expansions. The trace ideal gives exact module coefficient estimates, while the higher differential cycle remains required. Proof: Proposition 13.30a and Corollary 13.30b, equations 13.103a-13.103h. Human-source context: Connes 1986, Remark 7.16(a).

g.text: One intrinsic trace on the original crossed linking algebra
Y = Vₖ → X = V₁. The density, full corners and coefficient estimates retain the group action.
A. The two-step metric supplies an invariant base density
Vertical metric: tr(q⁻¹a q⁻¹b)
Quotient metric: q on TᵥV
Adapted derivative = [ orthogonal * ; 0 orthogonal ] ⇒ g*νₓ = νₓ
Different horizontal complements have triangular determinant 1. No invariant splitting.
n = 1: q = p⁻²dy², dνₓ = 2|dy dp|/p². This fixes the existing factor-two trace.
B. Full corners are restrictions of the same crossed trace
P C P = K(E) ⋊ᵣ Γ
Q C Q = C₀(X) ⋊ᵣ Γ
C = L(E) ⋊ᵣ Γ
τ(Σ LgUg) = ∫ₓ Tr(Hₓ)(Le(x)) dνₓ ; Hₓ = L²(Yₓ,μₓ) ⊕ ℂ
Top: ∫ₓ∫Yₓ Ke(y,y) dμₓ(y) dνₓ(x)
Bottom: ∫ₓ fe(x) dνₓ(x)
τ(Ξ*Ξ) = τ(ΞΞ*) for Ξ ∈ P C Q. Corners P,Q are invariant; fiber vectors may move.
C. Compact smooth kernels have an actual trace norm
TK(x) = Σp,q cpq(x) θvp,vq
f = dim Yₓ. Two summable lattice sums give ∫ₓ ‖TK(x)‖₁ dνₓ < ∞.
The diagonal trace is proved by this absolute Fourier sum, not by a formal diagonal rule.
D. The ideal controls coefficients; the differential step is still required
‖a T b‖₁ ≤ ‖a‖ ‖T‖₁ ‖b‖ ; τ(aT) = τ(Ta)
‖Ξ a‖₁ ≤ ‖Ξ‖₁ ‖a‖Aₓ ≤ ‖Ξ‖₁ ‖a‖B ; matrices and represented external units.
Counterexample: C₂ swaps two base points with weights 1,2; τ(aa*)=1 ≠ 2=τ(a*a).
Still required: characteristic differential cycle, differentiated-factor ideal bounds and pairing.
Exact proof: (13.103a)–(13.103h). The characteristic differential transfer remains required.
Human-source context: Connes (1986), Remark 7.16(a), PDF p.77. Original argument and diagram.
